## Description

SbobinAI transcribes long local audio and video recordings on your own NVIDIA GPU: speech detection cuts the audio at pauses, a local model transcribes each chunk, and you get TXT, Markdown, SRT, VTT and JSON plus a run report. Nothing leaves your machine.

Typical workflow:

1. `setup` download the pinned models into a resource store
2. `init-config` write config.local.toml pointing at that store
3. `doctor` verify FFmpeg, speech detector and backend
4. `run` | wizard  transcribe the files in input/
5. `read` output   output/<source>/<version>/transcript.txt, catalog.json

- Configuration: pass --config PATH (for example config.local.toml). There is no automatic discovery; without --config the built-in defaults are used. Command line options override the file; the file overrides the defaults.
- Non-interactive by default: only `wizard` (and `setup` without --yes) ever prompt. Use --json for machine-readable output.
- Running `sbobinai` with no command, or starting with an option, runs `run`.

## Options per command

### run

Transcribe the media files in the input folder (unattended).

```text
sbobinai run [options]
```

Discovers media files in --input-dir (or takes the files given with --file), prepares the audio, detects speech, sends chunks to the configured backend and writes transcripts and reports under --output-dir. It never asks questions; it is the command for scripts and agents.
Each combination of file and settings is a version. Re-running skips versions that are already complete and resumes incomplete ones; --force recomputes. A fully transcribed queued source is archived to --processed-dir unless --no-archive-inputs.

**Inputs**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--file PATH` | Process this media file instead of discovering --input-dir; repeatable. Files outside the input folder are transcribed but never archived. Repeatable. |  |
| `--limit N` | Process at most N of the discovered files (a positive integer; run only). [default: all files] |  |
| `--max-duration SECONDS` | Transcribe only the first SECONDS of each file (a bounded quick check). It creates a separate version and keeps the input file in place. [default: unlimited] | `max_duration` |
| `--max-file-size BYTES` | Reject input files larger than BYTES (the job is recorded as failed). [default: unlimited] | `max_file_size` |
| `--sample-rate HZ` | Sample rate in Hz of the mono audio FFmpeg extracts for the model. [default: 16000] | `sample_rate` |

**Transcription**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--language CODE` | Spoken language code (for example it, en, de) or auto for no hint. Qwen3-ASR constrains its output to it unless --no-force-language. [default: auto (no hint)] | `language` |
| `--chunk-seconds SECONDS` | Maximum chunk length in seconds; the speech detector cuts at pauses and never exceeds it. Subtitle times are chunk boundaries, not word timings. [default: 15.0] | `chunk_seconds` |
| `--prompt TEXT` | Context or instructions sent with every chunk (topic, names, jargon); overrides the built-in prompt. Part of the version identity. [default: built-in transcript-only prompt] | `prompt` |
| `--prompt-file PATH` | Read the prompt from a UTF-8 file; mutually exclusive with --prompt. |  |
| `--response-mode {json,plain,qwen3-asr}` | How the model is asked to answer: json or plain for generic models, qwen3-asr for Qwen3-ASR GGUF on llama.cpp. [default: json] | `response_mode` |
| `--temperature T` | Sampling temperature, 0 to 2 (0 is greedy and reproducible). [default: 0.0] | `temperature` |
| `--seed N` | Sampling seed, 0 to 4294967295. [default: 42] | `seed` |
| `--max-tokens N` | Upper bound of generated tokens per chunk (llama.cpp). [default: 1024] | `max_tokens` |
| `--min-tokens N` | Token cap floor per chunk: cap = min(max-tokens, min-tokens + tokens-per-second * chunk seconds). [default: 48] | `min_tokens` |
| `--tokens-per-second RATE` | Token allowance per second of audio in the per-chunk cap (see --min-tokens). [default: 8.0] | `tokens_per_second` |
| `--compression-ratio-threshold RATIO` | Whisper-style gzip compression ratio above which a transcript counts as a loop and triggers the recovery ladder. [default: 2.4] | `compression_ratio_threshold` |
| `--repeat-penalty X` | llama.cpp repetition penalty; 1.0 disables it. [default: 1.0] | `repeat_penalty` |
| `--dry-multiplier X` | llama.cpp DRY sampler multiplier; 0 disables it. [default: 0.0] | `dry_multiplier` |
| `--force-language, --no-force-language` | Qwen3-ASR: constrain output to --language instead of auto-detection (--no-force-language disables). [default: true] | `force_language` |
| `--collect-logprobs, --no-collect-logprobs` | Request token log-probabilities for the uncalibrated confidence proxy (--no-collect-logprobs keeps responses small and faster). [default: true] | `collect_logprobs` |
| `--parallel-requests N` | Concurrent chunk requests, 1 to 8; must not exceed the server parallel slots. Values above 1 create a distinct version. [default: 1] | `parallel_requests` |

**Speech detection**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--vad {silero,energy,none}` | Speech detector: silero (ONNX model file), energy (FFmpeg only) or none (fixed-length chunks, silence reaches the model). [default: silero] | `vad` |
| `--vad-model-path PATH` | Silero ONNX model file; a relative config value resolves against [resources].store. [default: models/silero_vad.onnx] | `vad_model_path` |
| `--vad-threshold P` | Speech probability threshold, greater than 0 and less than 1. [default: 0.5] | `vad_threshold` |
| `--vad-min-speech-seconds SECONDS` | Discard speech segments shorter than SECONDS. [default: 0.25] | `vad_min_speech_seconds` |
| `--vad-min-silence-seconds SECONDS` | Minimum silence in seconds that ends a speech segment. [default: 0.1] | `vad_min_silence_seconds` |
| `--vad-speech-pad-seconds SECONDS` | Padding in seconds added around each speech segment. [default: 0.2] | `vad_speech_pad_seconds` |
| `--vad-max-merge-gap-seconds SECONDS` | Merge neighbouring segments separated by less than SECONDS (within the chunk limit). [default: 1.0] | `vad_max_merge_gap_seconds` |
| `--vad-energy-margin-db DB` | Energy detector only: dB above the noise floor that counts as speech. [default: 15.0] | `vad_energy_margin_db` |

**Recovery**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--fallback-temperatures LIST` | Comma-separated temperatures (0 to 2) retried after degenerate output; an empty value disables them. Example: 0.2,0.4 [default: 0.2,0.4] | `fallback_temperatures` |
| `--split-on-failure, --no-split-on-failure` | Split a still-failing chunk once at its quietest pause (--no-split-on-failure disables). [default: true] | `split_on_failure` |
| `--context-free-fallback, --no-context-free-fallback` | Retry a chunk without the prompt/context when the model echoed it (--no-context-free-fallback disables). [default: true] | `context_free_fallback` |
| `--retries N` | Extra attempts after a transient request failure, 0 or more (not part of the version identity). [default: 2] | `retries` |

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ui {auto,live,plain,jsonl}` | Console output: live (progress display), plain (status lines), jsonl (event stream on stdout) or auto (live only on an interactive terminal). [default: auto] | `ui` |
| `--monitor, --no-monitor` | Sample CPU, RAM and NVIDIA GPU use during the run (--no-monitor disables). [default: true] | `monitor` |
| `--monitor-interval SECONDS` | Seconds between resource samples, 0.1 to 3600. [default: 1.0] | `monitor_interval` |
| `--intermediate-interval-seconds SECONDS` | Minimum seconds between rewrites of the intermediate exports; 0 rewrites after every chunk. The checkpoint is always written per chunk. [default: 10.0] | `intermediate_interval_seconds` |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Server/runtime**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--backend {nexa,mock,llamacpp}` | Inference backend: llamacpp (local llama-server over HTTP), nexa (historical Nexa runtime) or mock (tests; never real transcripts). [default: nexa] | `backend` |
| `--model NAME` | Model name: the llama-server alias for llamacpp. Default depends on the backend (qwen2-audio-7b for llamacpp, qwen2audio for nexa, mock for mock). [default: depends on backend] | `model` |
| `--base-url URL` | llama.cpp server base URL, for example http://127.0.0.1:8088. [default: http://127.0.0.1:8088] | `base_url` |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | llama.cpp request timeout in seconds. [default: 180.0] | `timeout` |
| `--device NAME` | Device name passed to the legacy Nexa backend (auto, cuda, ...). [default: auto] | `device` |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Path to a TOML configuration file (for example config.local.toml). Optional: there is no automatic discovery, so without it the built-in defaults apply. Every other option overrides the same-named key of this file. |  |
| `--input-dir DIR` | Operational queue: media files waiting to be transcribed. [default: input] | `input_dir` |
| `--process-dir DIR` | Working files, checkpoints, raw model responses and run logs. [default: process] | `process_dir` |
| `--processed-dir DIR` | Archive for fully transcribed queued sources. [default: processed] | `processed_dir` |
| `--output-dir DIR` | Results: transcripts, reports, source.json and catalog.json. [default: output] | `output_dir` |
| `--ffmpeg EXE` | FFmpeg executable name or path. [default: ffmpeg] | `ffmpeg` |
| `--ffprobe EXE` | FFprobe executable name or path. [default: ffprobe] | `ffprobe` |
| `--model-path PATH` | Existing local model file for the legacy Nexa backend (no download). [default: unset] | `model_path` |
| `--projector-path PATH` | Existing local audio projector file required by the legacy Nexa backend. [default: unset] | `projector_path` |

**Behaviour**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force, --no-force` | Recompute versions that are already complete instead of skipping them (--no-force restores the default). [default: false] | `force` |
| `--prepare-only, --no-prepare-only` | Only probe, detect speech and cut chunks; no model is contacted and nothing is archived. [default: false] | `prepare_only` |
| `--archive-inputs, --no-archive-inputs` | Move fully transcribed queued sources to --processed-dir (--no-archive-inputs keeps them in the input folder). [default: true] | `archive_inputs` |
| `--watch-interval SECONDS` | watch: seconds between scans of the input folder. [default: 5.0] | `watch_interval` |
| `--stable-scans N` | watch: scans, at least 2, a file must keep its size and mtime before it is processed (avoids half-copied files). [default: 2] | `stable_scans` |

Notes:

- Options override the configuration file; the file overrides the defaults. Anything not part of job identity (paths, ui, monitor, retries) never creates a new version.
- With no command at all, or when the first word is an option, sbobinai runs `run`.
- A job that cannot transcribe some chunks ends `incomplete`: the partial result lists the gaps, the file stays in the input folder and exit status is 1.

Files:

- input/ (queue), output/<source>/<version>/ (results), process/ (working files), processed/ (archive), process/runs/<run-id>/ (events, status, log).

With `--json`: stdout is JSON Lines: one event per line (see EVENTS) ending with {"type": "result", "schema_version": 1, "ok": bool, "command": "run", "exit_status": N, "jobs": [{"job_id", "source", "status", "transcript"?, "error"?}]} and, when not ok, an "error" object with code job_failed or job_incomplete.

Examples:

```text
# Transcribe everything in input/ with your local settings
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml

# One file, Italian, keep it in place
Windows: sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --file input\talk.mp4 --language it --no-archive-inputs
POSIX:   sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --file input/talk.mp4 --language it --no-archive-inputs

# Quick check of the first 10 minutes (separate version)
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --max-duration 600 --limit 1

# Validate preparation only (no model needed)
sbobinai run --prepare-only --vad energy --limit 1

# Stream machine events, then read the result line
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --json

# Recompute an already finished version
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --file input/talk.mp4 --force
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Every job completed, was skipped as already done, or was prepared only. |
| 1 | A job failed or ended incomplete, the backend is unavailable, or another sbobinai process holds the lock. |
| 2 | Invalid option, configuration file or prompt file. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl+C; re-run to resume. |

See also: [`watch`](#watch), [`wizard`](#wizard), [`doctor`](#doctor), [`events`](#events), [`catalog`](#catalog)

### watch

Keep watching the input folder and transcribe new files.

```text
sbobinai watch [options]
```

Scans --input-dir every --watch-interval seconds and processes files whose size and modification time stayed unchanged for --stable-scans scans, so half-copied files are not read. Runs until Ctrl+C.
Use it for a drop folder on a workstation. For one-off batches prefer `run`.

Files:

With `--json`: Events stream as JSON Lines; after Ctrl+C a {"type": "result", "command": "watch", "ok": true, "exit_status": 0} line is written.

Examples:

```text
# Watch the input folder until Ctrl+C
sbobinai watch --config config.local.toml

# Scan every 10 s, require 3 stable scans, plain output
sbobinai watch --config config.local.toml --watch-interval 10 --stable-scans 3 --ui plain
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Stopped with Ctrl+C (the normal way to end a watch). |
| 1 | Backend unavailable or another sbobinai process holds the lock. |
| 2 | Invalid option or configuration file (--file and --limit are not supported by watch). |

See also: [`run`](#run), [`events`](#events)

### wizard

Guided interactive run: asks language, context and scope.

```text
sbobinai wizard [options]
```

Shows the queue with durations and an estimate, asks the spoken language, optional context and scope (whole file or first N minutes), confirms, runs and prints a results table. Your last answers are remembered. The only command that asks questions.
It needs an interactive terminal. For automation pass --answers with a JSON file; the questions are skipped.

**Inputs**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--file PATH` | Process this media file instead of discovering --input-dir; repeatable. Files outside the input folder are transcribed but never archived. Repeatable. |  |
| `--max-duration SECONDS` | Transcribe only the first SECONDS of each file (a bounded quick check). It creates a separate version and keeps the input file in place. [default: unlimited] | `max_duration` |
| `--max-file-size BYTES` | Reject input files larger than BYTES (the job is recorded as failed). [default: unlimited] | `max_file_size` |
| `--sample-rate HZ` | Sample rate in Hz of the mono audio FFmpeg extracts for the model. [default: 16000] | `sample_rate` |
| `--answers PATH` | JSON file with the answers (automation and tests); skips the questions. Keys: language, context, max_minutes, confirm. |  |

**Transcription**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--language CODE` | Spoken language code (for example it, en, de) or auto for no hint. Qwen3-ASR constrains its output to it unless --no-force-language. [default: auto (no hint)] | `language` |
| `--chunk-seconds SECONDS` | Maximum chunk length in seconds; the speech detector cuts at pauses and never exceeds it. Subtitle times are chunk boundaries, not word timings. [default: 15.0] | `chunk_seconds` |
| `--prompt TEXT` | Context or instructions sent with every chunk (topic, names, jargon); overrides the built-in prompt. Part of the version identity. [default: built-in transcript-only prompt] | `prompt` |
| `--prompt-file PATH` | Read the prompt from a UTF-8 file; mutually exclusive with --prompt. |  |
| `--response-mode {json,plain,qwen3-asr}` | How the model is asked to answer: json or plain for generic models, qwen3-asr for Qwen3-ASR GGUF on llama.cpp. [default: json] | `response_mode` |
| `--temperature T` | Sampling temperature, 0 to 2 (0 is greedy and reproducible). [default: 0.0] | `temperature` |
| `--seed N` | Sampling seed, 0 to 4294967295. [default: 42] | `seed` |
| `--max-tokens N` | Upper bound of generated tokens per chunk (llama.cpp). [default: 1024] | `max_tokens` |
| `--min-tokens N` | Token cap floor per chunk: cap = min(max-tokens, min-tokens + tokens-per-second * chunk seconds). [default: 48] | `min_tokens` |
| `--tokens-per-second RATE` | Token allowance per second of audio in the per-chunk cap (see --min-tokens). [default: 8.0] | `tokens_per_second` |
| `--compression-ratio-threshold RATIO` | Whisper-style gzip compression ratio above which a transcript counts as a loop and triggers the recovery ladder. [default: 2.4] | `compression_ratio_threshold` |
| `--repeat-penalty X` | llama.cpp repetition penalty; 1.0 disables it. [default: 1.0] | `repeat_penalty` |
| `--dry-multiplier X` | llama.cpp DRY sampler multiplier; 0 disables it. [default: 0.0] | `dry_multiplier` |
| `--force-language, --no-force-language` | Qwen3-ASR: constrain output to --language instead of auto-detection (--no-force-language disables). [default: true] | `force_language` |
| `--collect-logprobs, --no-collect-logprobs` | Request token log-probabilities for the uncalibrated confidence proxy (--no-collect-logprobs keeps responses small and faster). [default: true] | `collect_logprobs` |
| `--parallel-requests N` | Concurrent chunk requests, 1 to 8; must not exceed the server parallel slots. Values above 1 create a distinct version. [default: 1] | `parallel_requests` |

**Speech detection**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--vad {silero,energy,none}` | Speech detector: silero (ONNX model file), energy (FFmpeg only) or none (fixed-length chunks, silence reaches the model). [default: silero] | `vad` |
| `--vad-model-path PATH` | Silero ONNX model file; a relative config value resolves against [resources].store. [default: models/silero_vad.onnx] | `vad_model_path` |
| `--vad-threshold P` | Speech probability threshold, greater than 0 and less than 1. [default: 0.5] | `vad_threshold` |
| `--vad-min-speech-seconds SECONDS` | Discard speech segments shorter than SECONDS. [default: 0.25] | `vad_min_speech_seconds` |
| `--vad-min-silence-seconds SECONDS` | Minimum silence in seconds that ends a speech segment. [default: 0.1] | `vad_min_silence_seconds` |
| `--vad-speech-pad-seconds SECONDS` | Padding in seconds added around each speech segment. [default: 0.2] | `vad_speech_pad_seconds` |
| `--vad-max-merge-gap-seconds SECONDS` | Merge neighbouring segments separated by less than SECONDS (within the chunk limit). [default: 1.0] | `vad_max_merge_gap_seconds` |
| `--vad-energy-margin-db DB` | Energy detector only: dB above the noise floor that counts as speech. [default: 15.0] | `vad_energy_margin_db` |

**Recovery**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--fallback-temperatures LIST` | Comma-separated temperatures (0 to 2) retried after degenerate output; an empty value disables them. Example: 0.2,0.4 [default: 0.2,0.4] | `fallback_temperatures` |
| `--split-on-failure, --no-split-on-failure` | Split a still-failing chunk once at its quietest pause (--no-split-on-failure disables). [default: true] | `split_on_failure` |
| `--context-free-fallback, --no-context-free-fallback` | Retry a chunk without the prompt/context when the model echoed it (--no-context-free-fallback disables). [default: true] | `context_free_fallback` |
| `--retries N` | Extra attempts after a transient request failure, 0 or more (not part of the version identity). [default: 2] | `retries` |

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ui {auto,live,plain,jsonl}` | Console output: live (progress display), plain (status lines), jsonl (event stream on stdout) or auto (live only on an interactive terminal). [default: auto] | `ui` |
| `--monitor, --no-monitor` | Sample CPU, RAM and NVIDIA GPU use during the run (--no-monitor disables). [default: true] | `monitor` |
| `--monitor-interval SECONDS` | Seconds between resource samples, 0.1 to 3600. [default: 1.0] | `monitor_interval` |
| `--intermediate-interval-seconds SECONDS` | Minimum seconds between rewrites of the intermediate exports; 0 rewrites after every chunk. The checkpoint is always written per chunk. [default: 10.0] | `intermediate_interval_seconds` |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Server/runtime**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--backend {nexa,mock,llamacpp}` | Inference backend: llamacpp (local llama-server over HTTP), nexa (historical Nexa runtime) or mock (tests; never real transcripts). [default: nexa] | `backend` |
| `--model NAME` | Model name: the llama-server alias for llamacpp. Default depends on the backend (qwen2-audio-7b for llamacpp, qwen2audio for nexa, mock for mock). [default: depends on backend] | `model` |
| `--base-url URL` | llama.cpp server base URL, for example http://127.0.0.1:8088. [default: http://127.0.0.1:8088] | `base_url` |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | llama.cpp request timeout in seconds. [default: 180.0] | `timeout` |
| `--device NAME` | Device name passed to the legacy Nexa backend (auto, cuda, ...). [default: auto] | `device` |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Path to a TOML configuration file (for example config.local.toml). Optional: there is no automatic discovery, so without it the built-in defaults apply. Every other option overrides the same-named key of this file. |  |
| `--input-dir DIR` | Operational queue: media files waiting to be transcribed. [default: input] | `input_dir` |
| `--process-dir DIR` | Working files, checkpoints, raw model responses and run logs. [default: process] | `process_dir` |
| `--processed-dir DIR` | Archive for fully transcribed queued sources. [default: processed] | `processed_dir` |
| `--output-dir DIR` | Results: transcripts, reports, source.json and catalog.json. [default: output] | `output_dir` |
| `--ffmpeg EXE` | FFmpeg executable name or path. [default: ffmpeg] | `ffmpeg` |
| `--ffprobe EXE` | FFprobe executable name or path. [default: ffprobe] | `ffprobe` |
| `--model-path PATH` | Existing local model file for the legacy Nexa backend (no download). [default: unset] | `model_path` |
| `--projector-path PATH` | Existing local audio projector file required by the legacy Nexa backend. [default: unset] | `projector_path` |

**Behaviour**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force, --no-force` | Recompute versions that are already complete instead of skipping them (--no-force restores the default). [default: false] | `force` |
| `--prepare-only, --no-prepare-only` | Only probe, detect speech and cut chunks; no model is contacted and nothing is archived. [default: false] | `prepare_only` |
| `--archive-inputs, --no-archive-inputs` | Move fully transcribed queued sources to --processed-dir (--no-archive-inputs keeps them in the input folder). [default: true] | `archive_inputs` |
| `--watch-interval SECONDS` | watch: seconds between scans of the input folder. [default: 5.0] | `watch_interval` |
| `--stable-scans N` | watch: scans, at least 2, a file must keep its size and mtime before it is processed (avoids half-copied files). [default: 2] | `stable_scans` |

Notes:

- Answers that change the output (language, context, scope) create a new version; earlier versions are kept.
- With --json the questions are not asked, --answers is required and the wizard's chatter goes to stderr.

Files:

- .local/wizard/last-answers.json (remembered answers), plus those of `run`.

With `--json`: Requires --answers. Events stream as JSON Lines, then {"type": "result", "command": "wizard", "ok": bool, "exit_status": N}.

Examples:

```text
# Interactive session
sbobinai wizard --config config.local.toml

# Scripted answers (no terminal needed)
sbobinai wizard --config config.local.toml --answers answers.json

# Only one file
Windows: sbobinai wizard --config config.local.toml --file input\talk.mp4
POSIX:   sbobinai wizard --config config.local.toml --file input/talk.mp4
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | All jobs completed or were skipped, or you cancelled before anything ran. |
| 1 | A job failed or ended incomplete, or another process holds the lock. |
| 2 | No terminal and no --answers, or an invalid answers file or answer. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl+C. |

See also: [`run`](#run), [`doctor`](#doctor)

### doctor

Check that FFmpeg, the speech detector and the backend are ready.

```text
sbobinai doctor [options]
```

Resolves the configuration like `run` does and verifies the media tools (ffmpeg, ffprobe), the speech detector and the transcription backend (for llamacpp: the server is reachable and the model loaded). Nothing is transcribed and no media is read.

- None written.

Examples:

```text
# Check the local configuration
sbobinai doctor --config config.local.toml

# Structured readiness for scripts and agents
sbobinai doctor --config config.local.toml --json

# Check a different backend without a config file
sbobinai doctor --backend mock --vad none
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Every check passed. |
| 1 | At least one check failed (details on stderr, or in the JSON checks). |
| 2 | Invalid option or configuration file. |

See also: [`setup`](#setup), [`init-config`](#init-config), [`run`](#run)

### events

Print a run's events as JSONL (tail -f style with --follow).

```text
sbobinai events [options]
```

Reads process/runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl and prints it line by line. With --follow it keeps polling until the run emits run.finished, so another terminal or an agent can watch a run in progress.
Events carry numbers and labels only, never transcript or prompt text.

**Inputs**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--run ID` | Run id (for example 20261002T211415Z-58da) or latest. [default: latest] |  |
| `--type PREFIX` | Only events whose type starts with this prefix (progress, chunk, job, run.finished, ...). |  |

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Path to a TOML configuration file (for example config.local.toml). Optional: there is no automatic discovery, so without it the built-in defaults apply. Every other option overrides the same-named key of this file. |  |
| `--process-dir DIR` | Folder holding runs/ (see run); default process. [default: process] | `process_dir` |

**Behaviour**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--follow` | Keep polling until the run emits run.finished. |  |

Files:

- process/runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl, process/runs/latest.json.

With `--json`: The output is already JSON Lines (one event per line); --json is accepted for uniformity and only makes errors structured.

Examples:

```text
# Follow the latest run until it finishes
sbobinai events --follow

# Only progress events of the latest run
sbobinai events --follow --type progress

# Replay a finished run
sbobinai events --run 20261002T211415Z-58da
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Events printed (also when stopped with Ctrl+C or a closed pipe). |
| 1 | No such run, or the run has no events file. |
| 2 | Invalid option or configuration file. |

See also: [`run`](#run), [`watch`](#watch)

### server-profile

Print the resolved [server] profile as JSON (absolute paths).

```text
sbobinai server-profile --config PATH [options]
```

Loads the configuration and prints the llama.cpp server profile (runtime, model and projector paths, alias, port, context size, slots, GPU layers, base URL) as one JSON object. The PowerShell launchers use it; agents can use it to learn how the local server is set up.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Path to the TOML configuration file (required). Required. |  |

**Behaviour**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--optional` | Print null and exit 0 when the configuration has no [server] table. |  |

With `--json`: The output is always one JSON object (or null); --json only structures errors.

Examples:

```text
# Show the server profile
sbobinai server-profile --config config.local.toml

# Tolerate a configuration without [server]
sbobinai server-profile --config config.local.toml --optional
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Profile (or null with --optional) printed. |
| 2 | Invalid configuration, or no [server] table without --optional. |

See also: [`init-config`](#init-config), [`doctor`](#doctor)

### init-config

Write a ready-to-use local configuration for a profile.

```text
sbobinai init-config --store DIR [options]
```

Renders config.example.toml for a profile of resources.json with all paths pointing into your resource store, validates the result and writes it (default config.local.toml, which is git-ignored). An existing file is never overwritten without --force.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--manifest PATH` | Path to resources.json. [default: resources.json next to the package] |  |
| `--store DIR` | Resource store folder for models, VAD and runtimes (required). Required. |  |
| `--output PATH` | File to write. [default: config.local.toml] |  |

**Behaviour**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--profile NAME` | Profile name from resources.json. [default: the manifest default profile] |  |
| `--force` | Overwrite an existing --output file. |  |

Files:

- Writes --output (default ./config.local.toml).

With `--json`: {"ok": true, "command": "init-config", "output", "profile", "store"}.

Examples:

```text
# Create config.local.toml for the default profile
Windows: sbobinai init-config --store D:\ai-models --profile qwen3-asr-1.7b-q8
POSIX:   sbobinai init-config --store ~/ai-models --profile qwen3-asr-1.7b-q8

# Regenerate it, replacing the old one
Windows: sbobinai init-config --store D:\ai-models --force
POSIX:   sbobinai init-config --store ~/ai-models --force
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | File written. |
| 1 | The output file exists (use --force). |
| 2 | Unknown profile, unreadable manifest or template, or invalid result. |

See also: [`setup`](#setup), [`doctor`](#doctor), [`server-profile`](#server-profile)

### setup

Download the pinned resources of a profile into the resource store.

```text
sbobinai setup [options]
```

Prints the plan (files, sizes, status) of a resources.json profile, asks for confirmation, downloads missing or partial files with resume, verifies size and SHA-256 and records provenance. Existing files that do not match are never overwritten. The llama.cpp runtime has its own installer; setup prints the command.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Local configuration providing [resources].store. |  |
| `--manifest PATH` | Path to resources.json. [default: resources.json next to the package] |  |
| `--store DIR` | Resource store folder (overrides [resources].store). |  |

**Behaviour**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--profile NAME` | Profile name from resources.json. [default: the manifest default profile] |  |
| `--yes` | Do not ask for confirmation. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Only print the plan; download nothing. |  |

Notes:

- With --json there is no prompt: pass --yes (or --dry-run).

Files:

- <store>/... downloaded files and their .provenance records.

With `--json`: {"ok": bool, "command": "setup", "profile", "store", "dry_run", "plan": [lines], "downloaded": [paths], "failed": [ids]}.

Examples:

```text
# Show the plan only
sbobinai setup --config config.local.toml --dry-run

# Download after confirming
sbobinai setup --config config.local.toml

# Unattended download with a JSON summary
sbobinai setup --config config.local.toml --yes --json
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Everything is installed (or the dry run found no conflict). |
| 1 | Conflict, not enough disk space, declined confirmation or a failed download. |
| 2 | No store, unknown profile or invalid configuration. |

See also: [`init-config`](#init-config), [`doctor`](#doctor)

### catalog

Rebuild catalog.json and every source.json from process/ and output/.

```text
sbobinai catalog [options]
```

Regenerates output/catalog.json and each output/<source>/source.json from the job metadata, newest first. It is normally kept up to date automatically; run it after moving folders by hand or after an interrupted run. Transcripts are not touched.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Path to a TOML configuration file (for example config.local.toml). Optional: there is no automatic discovery, so without it the built-in defaults apply. Every other option overrides the same-named key of this file. |  |
| `--input-dir DIR` | Operational queue: media files waiting to be transcribed. [default: input] | `input_dir` |
| `--process-dir DIR` | Working files, checkpoints, raw model responses and run logs. [default: process] | `process_dir` |
| `--processed-dir DIR` | Archive for fully transcribed queued sources. [default: processed] | `processed_dir` |
| `--output-dir DIR` | Results: transcripts, reports, source.json and catalog.json. [default: output] | `output_dir` |

Files:

- Writes output/catalog.json and output/<source>/source.json.

With `--json`: {"ok": true, "command": "catalog", "sources": N, "versions": N}.

Examples:

```text
# Rebuild the overview
sbobinai catalog --config config.local.toml

# Machine-readable summary
sbobinai catalog --config config.local.toml --json
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Catalog rebuilt. |
| 1 | Another process holds the lock or a file could not be written. |
| 2 | Invalid configuration. |

See also: [`migrate-layout`](#migrate-layout), [`run`](#run)

### migrate-layout

Move legacy flat job folders into the per-source layout (dry run).

```text
sbobinai migrate-layout [options]
```

Plans the move of old flat job folders into process/<source>/<version> and output/<source>/<version>. Without --apply only the plan is printed. Conflicting folders are refused, never overwritten; a move log is written and the catalog rebuilt.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Path to a TOML configuration file (for example config.local.toml). Optional: there is no automatic discovery, so without it the built-in defaults apply. Every other option overrides the same-named key of this file. |  |
| `--input-dir DIR` | Operational queue: media files waiting to be transcribed. [default: input] | `input_dir` |
| `--process-dir DIR` | Working files, checkpoints, raw model responses and run logs. [default: process] | `process_dir` |
| `--processed-dir DIR` | Archive for fully transcribed queued sources. [default: processed] | `processed_dir` |
| `--output-dir DIR` | Results: transcripts, reports, source.json and catalog.json. [default: output] | `output_dir` |

**Behaviour**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--apply` | Perform the moves; without it only the plan is printed. |  |

Files:

- Moves folders under process/ and output/, writes a move log, rebuilds the catalog.

With `--json`: {"ok": bool, "command": "migrate-layout", "dry_run", "plan": [lines], "to_migrate", "refused", "untouched", "migrated"?, "failed"?, "log"?}.

Examples:

```text
# Preview the migration
sbobinai migrate-layout --config config.local.toml

# Apply it
sbobinai migrate-layout --config config.local.toml --apply
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Plan printed, or every move succeeded. |
| 1 | At least one move failed, or the lock is held. |
| 2 | Invalid configuration. |

See also: [`catalog`](#catalog)

### help

Show the help of a command (same as `<command> --help`).

```text
sbobinai help [COMMAND] [options]
```

Without an argument it prints the overview; with a command name it prints exactly what `sbobinai <command> --help` prints.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Arguments**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMMAND` | Command to describe. |  |

With `--json`: Prints the machine-readable description of the command (see man --format json).

Examples:

```text
# Overview
sbobinai help

# Help of one command
sbobinai help run
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Help printed. |
| 2 | Unknown command. |

See also: [`man`](#man)

### man

Print the full manual (text, markdown, json or skill).

```text
sbobinai man [COMMAND] [options]
```

Prints the manual generated from the same source as --help: NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, COMMANDS, OPTIONS, CONFIGURATION, FILES, ENVIRONMENT, EXIT STATUS, ERRORS, EXAMPLES, AGENT USAGE and SEE ALSO. --format json is the machine-readable interface description; --format skill prints the SKILL.md agent manifest.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format {text,markdown,json,skill}` | Output format. [default: text] |  |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output: one JSON object on stdout (run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a {"type": "result"} object). Errors become {"ok": false, "error": {...}} on stdout and nothing human is written to stderr. |  |

**Arguments**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMMAND` | Limit the manual to one command. |  |

Notes:

- --json is a shortcut for --format json.

With `--json`: Same as --format json.

Examples:

```text
# Read the manual
sbobinai man

# Regenerate the committed reference
sbobinai man --format markdown > docs/cli-reference.md

# Interface description for tools
sbobinai man --format json

# Manual of one command
sbobinai man run
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Manual printed. |
| 2 | Unknown command or format. |

See also: [`help`](#help)

### repl

Interactive shell that runs the commands above with a remembered config.

```text
sbobinai repl [options]
```

Starts a small shell with a banner, a prompt and (where the platform provides readline) command history. Type any subcommand with its arguments, for example `doctor` or `run --limit 1`. The --config given to repl (or set with `config PATH`) is added to every command that accepts it. Built-ins: help [command], config [PATH], exit, quit.
Starting sbobinai with no arguments still runs `run`; the shell only starts with this command.

**Output and UI**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Run every command inside the shell with --json. |  |

**Paths**

| Option | Meaning | Config key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | Path to a TOML configuration file (for example config.local.toml). Optional: there is no automatic discovery, so without it the built-in defaults apply. Every other option overrides the same-named key of this file. |  |

With `--json`: Every command typed inside the shell runs with --json.

Examples:

```text
# Start the shell
sbobinai repl --config config.local.toml

# Scripted session
echo doctor | sbobinai repl --config config.local.toml
```

Exit status:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Shell ended (exit, quit or end of input). |

See also: [`help`](#help), [`run`](#run), [`doctor`](#doctor)

## Configuration

Settings live in a TOML file given with `--config`: an `[audio_transcript]` table (or top-level keys) plus optional `[resources]` and `[server]` tables. Unknown keys are errors. Command-line options override the file. **Job identity** says whether changing a value creates a new version of a result (yes) or only changes how the run behaves (no).

| Table | Key | Type | Default | CLI flag | Job identity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `input_dir` | path | input | `--input-dir` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `processed_dir` | path | processed | `--processed-dir` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `process_dir` | path | process | `--process-dir` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `output_dir` | path | output | `--output-dir` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `backend` | string | nexa | `--backend` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `model` | string | depends on backend | `--model` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `base_url` | string | http://127.0.0.1:8088 | `--base-url` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `timeout` | number | 180.0 | `--timeout` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `max_tokens` | integer | 1024 | `--max-tokens` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `prompt` | string or null | built-in transcript-only prompt | `--prompt` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `temperature` | number | 0.0 | `--temperature` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `seed` | integer | 42 | `--seed` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `response_mode` | string | json | `--response-mode` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `model_path` | path or null | unset | `--model-path` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `projector_path` | path or null | unset | `--projector-path` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `device` | string | auto | `--device` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `ffmpeg` | string | ffmpeg | `--ffmpeg` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `ffprobe` | string | ffprobe | `--ffprobe` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `language` | string or null | auto (no hint) | `--language` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `chunk_seconds` | number | 15.0 | `--chunk-seconds` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `sample_rate` | integer | 16000 | `--sample-rate` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `max_duration` | number or null | unlimited | `--max-duration` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `max_file_size` | integer or null | unlimited | `--max-file-size` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `retries` | integer | 2 | `--retries` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `force` | boolean | false | `--force/--no-force` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `prepare_only` | boolean | false | `--prepare-only/--no-prepare-only` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `archive_inputs` | boolean | true | `--archive-inputs/--no-archive-inputs` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `watch_interval` | number | 5.0 | `--watch-interval` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `stable_scans` | integer | 2 | `--stable-scans` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad` | string | silero | `--vad` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad_model_path` | path | models/silero_vad.onnx | `--vad-model-path` | yes (silero only) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad_threshold` | number | 0.5 | `--vad-threshold` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad_min_speech_seconds` | number | 0.25 | `--vad-min-speech-seconds` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad_min_silence_seconds` | number | 0.1 | `--vad-min-silence-seconds` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad_speech_pad_seconds` | number | 0.2 | `--vad-speech-pad-seconds` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad_max_merge_gap_seconds` | number | 1.0 | `--vad-max-merge-gap-seconds` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `vad_energy_margin_db` | number | 15.0 | `--vad-energy-margin-db` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `fallback_temperatures` | list of numbers | 0.2,0.4 | `--fallback-temperatures` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `split_on_failure` | boolean | true | `--split-on-failure/--no-split-on-failure` | yes |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `context_free_fallback` | boolean | true | `--context-free-fallback/--no-context-free-fallback` | yes (only when false) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `min_tokens` | integer | 48 | `--min-tokens` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `tokens_per_second` | number | 8.0 | `--tokens-per-second` | yes (llamacpp) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `compression_ratio_threshold` | number | 2.4 | `--compression-ratio-threshold` | yes (llamacpp) |

| `[audio_transcript]` | `parallel_requests` | integer | 1 | `--parallel-requests` | yes (llamacpp, only above 1) |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `intermediate_interval_seconds` | number | 10.0 | `--intermediate-interval-seconds` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `ui` | string | auto | `--ui` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `monitor` | boolean | true | `--monitor/--no-monitor` | no |
| `[audio_transcript]` | `monitor_interval` | number | 1.0 | `--monitor-interval` | no |
| `[resources]` | `store` | path | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `runtime_dir` | path | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `model_path` | path | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `projector_path` | path | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `alias` | string | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `state_dir` | path | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `port` | integer | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `context_size` | integer | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `parallel` | integer | required | file only | no |
| `[server]` | `gpu_layers` | integer | unset | file only | no |

## Files

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `input/` | Operational queue; failed, incomplete, bounded and prepare-only jobs stay. |
| `processed/<source>/<file>` | Original file after a complete transcription. |
| `process/<source>/<version>/` | Working files: chunks, checkpoint, metadata.json, raw responses, events.jsonl of that job. |
| `process/runs/<run-id>/` | events.jsonl, status.json and pipeline.log of one run. |
| `process/runs/latest.json` | Pointer to the latest run id and its state. |
| `process/.audio-transcript.lock` | Process lock: one run at a time. |
| `output/catalog.json` | Every input file, latest activity first. |
| `output/<source>/source.json` | All versions of one input, newest first. |
| `output/<source>/<version>/transcript.{txt,md,srt,vtt,json}` | The transcript. |
| `output/<source>/<version>/report.json` | Settings, timings, counts, confidence. |
| `output/<source>/<version>/run-report.md` | Human-readable report. |
| `output/<source>/<version>/intermediate/` | Partial results while a job runs. |
| `config.local.toml` | Your local configuration (git-ignored); see config.example.toml. |
| `.local/wizard/last-answers.json` | Answers remembered by the wizard. |

## Environment

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `NO_COLOR` | When set (any value), the live console uses no colors. |
| `CI` | When set, --ui auto never picks the live display (plain status lines). |
| `TERM` | TERM=dumb disables the live display under --ui auto. |
| `PATH` | Used to find ffmpeg and ffprobe when --ffmpeg/--ffprobe are plain names. |
| `SILERO_VAD_MODEL` | Tests only: Silero ONNX file for the optional real-model tests. |

## Exit status

| Code | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | success | Success: every job completed or was skipped as already done, the command finished, or the user cancelled before anything ran (wizard). Ctrl+C ending `watch` or `events --follow` is a normal stop and also returns 0. |
| 1 | failed | A job failed or ended incomplete, a check failed (doctor), a resource or runtime problem occurred (backend unavailable, another run holds the lock, no such run, download failure, output file exists). |
| 2 | usage | Usage or configuration error: unknown or invalid option, invalid or unreadable configuration or answers file, missing [server] table, wizard without a terminal. |
| 130 | interrupted | Interrupted by Ctrl+C during a run; job state stays recoverable. |

## Errors in JSON mode

With `--json` a failure is `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "exit_status": N}}` on stdout; stderr stays empty. The codes are stable.

| Code | Exit status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | 2 | Invalid command line (unknown command or option, bad value). |
| `config_invalid` | 2 | The configuration file or a value overriding it is invalid. |
| `answers_invalid` | 2 | The wizard answers file or an answer is invalid. |
| `interactive_required` | 2 | The wizard needs a terminal or --answers. |
| `server_not_configured` | 2 | The configuration has no [server] table. |
| `backend_unavailable` | 1 | The transcription backend or a tool it needs failed. |
| `lock_held` | 1 | Another sbobinai process holds the process lock. |
| `job_failed` | 1 | At least one job failed (see jobs[].error). |
| `job_incomplete` | 1 | At least one job ended incomplete; re-run to retry gaps. |
| `checks_failed` | 1 | doctor found at least one failing check. |
| `run_not_found` | 1 | events: no run exists (for example latest with no runs yet). |
| `events_missing` | 1 | events: the requested run id has no events file. |
| `config_exists` | 1 | init-config: the output file exists (use --force). |
| `resource_conflict` | 1 | setup: a file exists but does not match the pinned one. |
| `insufficient_space` | 1 | setup: not enough free disk space at the store. |
| `download_failed` | 1 | setup: at least one download failed verification. |
| `migration_failed` | 1 | migrate-layout: at least one job could not be moved. |
| `runtime_error` | 1 | Any other runtime error (message holds the details). |
| `interrupted` | 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl+C. |

## Events

| Type | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `run.started` | command, model, backend, response_mode, language, parallel_requests, queue_size, ui |
| `job.started` | source, version, scope, index, total |
| `stage.started` | stage |
| `stage.finished` | stage, seconds, reused? |
| `job.prepared` | analysed_seconds, speech_seconds, chunk_count, detector, reused |
| `chunk.started` | index, part, audio_seconds, in_flight |
| `chunk.attempt` | index, stage, temperature, outcome, wall_seconds, completion_tokens |
| `chunk.finished` | index, outcome, attempts, wall_seconds, running counters |
| `progress` | done_chunks, total_chunks, percent, eta_s, throughput_x, ok, failed |
| `resource.sample` | cpu_percent, ram_used_mb, gpu_util_percent, gpu_mem_used_mb, ... |
| `log` | level, message |
| `warning` | code, message |
| `job.finished` | source, status, counts, timings, confidence, artifacts, archived |
| `run.finished` | exit_status, jobs, wall_seconds |

Details: [events.md](events.md).

## Agent usage

- Non-interactive by default. Only `wizard` asks questions (needs a terminal or --answers) and `setup` confirms unless --yes; never call them without those.
- Use --json on every command. One-shot commands print one JSON object; run/watch/wizard stream JSON Lines events and end with a result object. `--ui jsonl` streams events without the result line; `--ui plain` gives stable text lines.
- Branch on the exit status (0, 1, 2, 130; see EXIT STATUS) and, in JSON mode, on error.code. Errors are {"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message", "exit_status"}} on stdout; stderr stays empty.
- Read results from files, not from console text: output/catalog.json (all sources), output/<source>/source.json (versions, newest first) and output/<source>/<version>/transcript.* and report.json.
- Idempotent: re-running skips versions that are already complete and resumes incomplete ones; --force recomputes. Different settings create a new version, never overwrite an old one.
- Bound the work with --file, --limit and --max-duration (a bounded run is a separate version and keeps the input file).
- Follow a run with `events --follow` (JSON Lines, ends at run.finished) or poll process/runs/latest.json and process/runs/<run-id>/status.json.
- One run at a time: a second process fails with exit status 1 (lock_held). Check readiness first with `doctor --json`; do not start or stop the model server yourself unless the user asks.

## Recipes

**Check readiness as JSON**

```sh
sbobinai doctor --config config.local.toml --json   # exit 0 and ok=true when ready
```

**Transcribe one file and print the transcript path**

```sh
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --json --file input/talk.mp4 \
  | tail -n 1 | jq -r '.jobs[0].transcript'
```

```powershell
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --json --file input\talk.mp4 |
  Select-Object -Last 1 | ConvertFrom-Json | ForEach-Object { $_.jobs[0].transcript }
```

**Branch on the outcome of a run**

```sh
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --json > run.jsonl; case $? in 0) echo done;;
  1) tail -n 1 run.jsonl | jq '.error';; 2) echo fix the command line;; esac
```

**List every transcribed source, latest activity first**

```sh
jq -r '.sources[] | [.original_name, .latest_version.status] | @tsv' output/catalog.json
```

```powershell
(Get-Content output\catalog.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).sources |
  ForEach-Object { "$($_.original_name) $($_.latest_version.status)" }
```

**List the versions of one source, newest first**

```sh
jq -r '.versions[] | [.version, .status, .completion_percent] | @tsv' \
  output/<source>/source.json
```

```powershell
(Get-Content output\<source>\source.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).versions |
  Select-Object version, status, completion_percent
```

**Follow progress of a running job until it finishes**

```sh
sbobinai events --follow --type progress     # ends after run.finished
```

**Quick bounded check: first 10 minutes, keep the file in input**

```sh
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --json --limit 1 --max-duration 600 --no-archive-inputs
```

**Recompute a version that is already complete**

```sh
sbobinai run --config config.local.toml --json --file input/talk.mp4 --force
```

**Preview a download without changing anything**

```sh
sbobinai setup --config config.local.toml --dry-run --json
```

**Learn how the local server is configured**

```sh
sbobinai server-profile --config config.local.toml --optional
```
